writableLeaves.currentText: Strongest feature: Evans directly separates final authorship from underlying provenance and supports a limited eyewitness core through living-memory dating, named and unnamed informants, Bauckham, and Taylor’s criticism. Principal limitation: The continued existence of witnesses does not demonstrate their practical supervision of dispersed traditions, and particular Gospel materials are not traced to particular witnesses within the move. Live burden: Evans must explain mechanisms of access, correction, and geographical reach, while Ehrman must show that expanding oral networks escaped meaningful localized control rather than merely universal oversight. Locked score: The 84 reflects strong coherence, evidence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and calibration, with no severely weak dimension, yet its bounded conclusion remains better supported than the broader implication that eyewitness survival effectively constrained transmitted stories.

sourceEvidence.speaker: Craig Evans
sourceEvidence.excerpt: the professor of New Testament at the University of St Andrews in Scotland has concluded that there is present in the New Testament gospels a substantial core of eyewitness tradition bacham has reminded us of Vincent Taylor's complaint of radical form critics long ago who assumed that most of the material in the gospel El both the sayings and the Deeds of Jesus were invented by the church as though there were no eyewitnesses present to check such fabrication Taylor makes the Ry comment quote if the form critics are right the disciples must have been translated carried up to heaven immediately after the resurrection bacham rightly reminds us that quote the gospels were written within living memory of the events that recount he argues that much of the material in the New Testament gospels can be traced to named and unnamed individuals who heard and observed Jesus including persons who met Jesus and were healed by him bacham is quite right form
sourceEvidence.proposition: A substantial Gospel core traces to identifiable eyewitnesses and was written within living memory, when fabrication could be checked.

responseComponents.text: Answers anonymous authorship by distinguishing authorship from the eyewitness provenance of underlying traditions.

writableLeaves.currentText: Strongest feature: Evans derives testable expectations from free invention, identifies conspicuously absent sayings addressing early controversies, and reinforces restraint through Paul’s explicit distinction between Jesus’s words and personal judgment. Principal limitation: Evidence against wholesale fabrication does not exclude gradual reshaping, selective preservation, or isolated invented sayings, while Papias’s precise Gospel links remain qualified and debatable. Live burden: Evans must show that these signs of restraint governed geographically dispersed transmission and protected contested material, whereas Ehrman must explain the missing dispute-tailored sayings under his change model. Locked score: The 88 rests on uniformly excellent coherence, evidence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and calibration, because the move supplies distinct empirical tests while candidly conceding editing, recontextualization, lost evidence, and uncertainty about Papias.

sourceEvidence.proposition: The absence of sayings tailored to early church disputes, Paul's source distinctions, and first-generation traditions weigh against wholesale invention of Jesus's words.

responseComponents.text: Appeals to Papias and first-generation written and oral materials as evidence of eyewitness-linked tradition despite anonymous texts.
Argues against uncontrolled invention because invented sayings do not address prominent church disputes and Paul distinguishes Jesus's words from his own.
